name: Cryogenic I-V, dark-count-rate and thermal-cycling qualification of 6x6 mm2 SiPMs at 77 K for a liquid-argon neutrino detector
plain_name: Qualify light sensors for a liquid-argon neutrino detector by dunking them in liquid nitrogen
description: DUNE photon-detection-system SiPM validation: sensors are lowered into a liquid-nitrogen dewar on a linear stage with a PT100 nearby, I-V curves are taken with a source-measure unit over triaxial cables, dark count rate, gain and correlated noise are recorded in the dark with a cryogenic amplifier, and the sensors undergo 20 room-temperature/LN2 thermal cycles.
keywords: Qualify light sensors for a liquid-argon neutrino detector by dunking them in liquid nitrogen

sources.citation: Cryogenic characterization of FBK NUV-HD-Cryo 3T SiPM sensors for the DUNE photon detection system (arXiv:2511.19095v1)

reported_equipment: liquid nitrogen (LN2) dewar with mechanical linear stage

requirements.rationale: DCR and noise specifications are verified at 77 K.
Sensors are immersed (dived) in liquid nitrogen.
Bias and signal leads (triaxial cables to the SMU, cryogenic amplifier) must reach the sensor.
A 6x6 mm2 sensor has a circumscribed diameter of 8.5 mm.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
